record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Find the weakest possible regularity assumptions under which a Lorentzian metric can be considered a vacuum solution of the Einstein equations, including the distributional case where the metric and inverse are essentially bounded and first derivatives are square-integrable, and determine the optimal coordinates or differentiable structure for such a metric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold. Consider the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ in their weakest possible sense. Concretely, address the following: 

(1) Identify the minimal regularity class for a Lorentzian metric $g$ under which the Ricci tensor $\mathrm{Ric}(g)$ can be defined as a tensor distribution and the equation $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ makes rigorous distributional sense. In particular, investigate the borderline case in which both $g$ and its inverse $g^{-1}$ lie in $L^{\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(M)$ while the first partial derivatives of $g$ lie in $L^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(M)$, so that the nonlinear terms $g^{-1}(\partial g)(\partial g)$ appearing in the curvature can be interpreted via products of an $L^{\infty}$ function with $L^{2}$ functions.

(2) Determine the optimal choice of coordinates (e.g.\ wave/harmonic coordinates, Coulomb-type gauges, geodesic normal coordinates) and of underlying differentiable structure on $M$ that realises this minimal regularity, i.e.\ such that, after a suitable change of $C^{k}$-atlas, the metric attains the lowest possible regularity threshold for which the vacuum equations are well defined and for which a meaningful Cauchy problem and well-posedness theory can be developed.

State and prove (or disprove) a theorem giving such an optimal regularity class together with the corresponding coordinate/atlas selection, or show obstructions ruling out any further weakening.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a long-standing program rather than a single theorem. Major progress has been made: the bounded $L^2$ curvature theorem of Klainerman–Rodnianski–Szeftel (Invent. Math. 2015) establishes well-posedness of the vacuum Einstein equations assuming only an $L^2$ bound on the curvature, which corresponds essentially to $H^2$ regularity of the metric and is critical with respect to the causal geometry. Subsequent work (e.g. the localised bounded $L^2$-curvature theorem, and the spacelike-characteristic Cauchy problem in low regularity, 2022) has extended the theory. However, the genuinely distributional regime in which $g, g^{-1}\in L^\infty$ and $\partial g\in L^2$, and the determination of an optimal coordinate/differentiable structure achieving the weakest possible regularity, remain not fully resolved. The problem is therefore partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The bounded L^2 curvature conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Time of existence of a classical solution to the Einstein-vacuum equations depends only on the L2-norm of the curvature and a lower bound on the volume radius.
status_evidence.claim: Well-posedness of vacuum Einstein equations under only L^2 curvature bounds is established.

status_evidence.title: The Spacelike-Characteristic Cauchy Problem of General Relativity in Low Regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Low-regularity well-posedness results extending the bounded L^2 curvature theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Further progress on low-regularity vacuum Einstein theory continues, indicating the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Global weak solutions of 3+1 dimensional vacuum Einstein equations
status_evidence.snippet: Weak solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations are constructed in 3+1 dimensions under suitable foliations.
status_evidence.claim: Distributional/weak solutions are being actively studied but a full optimal regularity theorem is not established.
